# loopai

loopai is a local Go CLI that executes Markdown implementation plans task by task through Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, validates and commits each task, then runs configurable internal and external reviews.

## Install

This fork is distributed from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/echeg/loopai
cd loopai
make build
install -d ~/.local/bin
install -m 0755 .bin/loopai ~/.local/bin/loopai
loopai --version
```

Requirements:

- Go 1.26+
- Git
- Claude Code CLI for the default executor, or Codex CLI 0.130.0+ with `--codex`
- Optional second provider for cross-provider external review
- Optional fzf, cmux, and golangci-lint
- Optional for `--pr`: authenticated GitHub CLI and a GitHub remote named `origin`

Run loopai from a Git repository root.

## Claude Code plugin

Install the optional Claude Code workflows from this repository's marketplace:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add echeg/loopai
claude plugin install loopai@loopai
```

The plugin provides `loopai:loopai`, `loopai:loopai-plan`,
`loopai:loopai-brainstorm`, `loopai:loopai-adopt`, `loopai:loopai-update`, and
`loopai:loopai-grill`. The CLI remains the execution
engine. `loopai:loopai-grill` critiques an existing plan with Claude and Codex;
its `compare` mode generates, judges, and synthesizes competing plans.

Invoke `/loopai:loopai-grill [docs/plans/X.md]` for an active-plan critique or
`/loopai:loopai-grill compare <description-or-active-plan>` for a plan-off.
Grill mode continues Claude-only when Codex is unavailable; compare mode
requires Codex and stops without creating a plan. Neither mode accepts completed,
symlinked, or `.loopai/` plans, and final plan creation never overwrites an
existing path. Active-plan replacement is identity-and-content guarded and uses
no-clobber publication so concurrent writers are preserved. The skill
pre-approves no tools and runs Codex against a read-confined snapshot containing
only tracked and non-ignored untracked regular files without symlink components.
Python 3 and Git are required for deterministic path checks and snapshot creation.

Use `loopai:loopai-brainstorm` when a feature needs design exploration. It asks
one question at a time, compares approaches, and seeks section-by-section
approval. It then invokes `loopai:loopai-plan`, which records the approved
context, chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and verified facts in the
plan's `## Decisions` section. This pipeline does not create an intermediate
spec file or invoke `superpowers:writing-plans`.

Superpowers may remain installed for its other skills. When migrating from the
upstream ralphex plugin, run `claude plugin uninstall ralphex` and
`claude plugin marketplace remove ralphex` after installing loopai. In shared
projects, a `CLAUDE.md` directive can require plan creation through
`loopai:loopai-brainstorm` and `loopai:loopai-plan` instead of
`superpowers:writing-plans`.

## Core commands

```bash
loopai docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --plan "add a health-check endpoint"
loopai --tasks-only docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --review
loopai --external-only
loopai --codex docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --codex --pass-claude-md docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --codex --codex-args '-c service_tier="default"' docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --worktree docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --worktree --commit docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --serve docs/plans/feature.md
loopai --clear
loopai --merge
loopai --merge=release/13
loopai --merge dynamic-review-agents
loopai --merge 20260806-dynamic-review-agents
loopai --merge docs/plans/20260806-dynamic-review-agents.md
loopai --merge=release/13 dynamic-review-agents
loopai --pr
loopai --pr=release/13
loopai --pr dynamic-review-agents
loopai --gen-agents
loopai --init
loopai --reset
loopai --dump-defaults /tmp/loopai-defaults
```

Use `loopai --help` for all flags.

## Plan format

```markdown
# Plan: Add feature

## Overview

Describe the outcome.

## Validation Commands

- `go test ./...`
- `golangci-lint run`

### Task 1: Implement feature

- [ ] Add implementation
- [ ] Add tests
- [ ] Run validation
```

Task headings must be `### Task N:` or `### Iteration N:`. Incomplete work uses `[ ]`; loopai marks successful work `[x]`. Put actionable checkboxes inside task sections and include validation commands.

## Execution

The full pipeline is:

1. execute the first incomplete task in a fresh primary-executor session
2. validate, mark it complete, and commit
3. repeat for remaining tasks
4. run the first internal multi-agent review
5. run external findings review and primary-executor evaluation/fixes
6. run a final critical/major review
7. optionally finalize and move the plan to `docs/plans/completed/`

Claude Code is primary by default. `--codex` makes Codex primary for planning, task execution, internal review, fixes, and finalize. `external_review_tool = auto` selects the other installed provider. Set it to `none` to disable the legacy review path when `external_reviewers` is unset.

`--codex-args`, or `codex_args` in config, appends extra arguments to every codex invocation loopai spawns, covering both `--codex` phases and external codex review under a Claude primary. They are strictly additive, unlike `claude_args`, which is the claude command's whole argument list, and are appended after loopai's own `-c` overrides, so an explicit `-c` value there wins on key collision. Example: `codex_args = -c service_tier="default"` keeps long autonomous runs off the priority tier while interactive codex sessions keep `service_tier = "priority"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`. An explicit `--codex-args=` clears an inherited value; unset leaves codex invocations unchanged, and the `codex-as-claude.sh` wrapper path is unaffected. Caveats: the value is tokenized like a shell word list and quotes are removed, so a `-c` value whose TOML type depends on quoting must escape them (`-c project_doc_fallback_filenames=[\"CLAUDE.md\"]`) or codex fails to load its config; last-occurrence-wins covers `-c key=value` only, so repeating a typed flag loopai already passes (`--sandbox`) is a fatal codex parse error rather than an override; a bare positional token becomes `codex exec`'s prompt and silently discards loopai's; and extras also reach the read-only external codex reviewer, where `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` grants it write access.

For an ordered chain, configure `external_reviewers = codex:gpt-5.5:xhigh, claude:fable:max` using `provider[:model[:effort]]` entries. It takes precedence over `external_review_tool` and `external_review_model`; an empty local value or `--external-reviewers=` clears/disables an inherited chain. Reviewers run sequentially until clean, their per-reviewer iteration cap, or their per-reviewer stalemate threshold; they only report findings, while the primary executor evaluates and fixes them with `review_model` (falling back to `task_model`). Bare `claude` defaults to `opus:xhigh`; bare `codex` uses the configured Codex defaults, and Codex ignores `max` effort with a warning. Providers may repeat, with each entry creating a separate loop. Providers are `claude`, `codex`, and `custom`; a `custom` entry cannot include a model, requires `custom_review_script`, and repeated custom entries share that script.

## Configuration and data

Global config:

```text
~/.config/loopai/
```

Project config and runtime data:

```text
.loopai/
├── config
├── prompts/
├── agents/
├── progress/
└── worktrees/
```

Local files override global files, which override embedded defaults. `LOOPAI_CONFIG_DIR` or `--config-dir` overrides the global location. Old `~/.config/ralphex/` and `.ralphex/` directories are intentionally ignored.

## Review agents

Agents are plain-text review instructions in `agents/*.txt`, optionally prefixed with YAML frontmatter (`model`, `agent`, `description`). The internal first review always launches the five built-in agents: quality, implementation, testing, simplification, documentation.

An agent file with a non-empty `description` is a dynamic agent. Dynamic agents need no prompt edit: `review_first.txt` expands `{{agents:dynamic}}` into a catalog of them, and the primary executor picks the ones relevant to the diff (typically 0-3) and launches them in the same parallel message as the built-in five. Selecting none is valid. Agents without a description are only invoked through an explicit `{{agent:name}}` reference. Quote the description: the frontmatter is YAML, an unquoted value containing `: ` makes the block unparsable (indistinguishable from having no frontmatter), and an unquoted ` #` starts a YAML comment that truncates the description. A customized `review_first.txt` that lacks the `{{agents:dynamic}}` placeholder disables dynamic agents; the first review iteration logs a warning naming the dropped agents, and there is no other signal. An invalid `model` value drops the execution overrides for that agent but keeps its `description`, so it still appears in the catalog.

`loopai --gen-agents` runs one executor session that analyzes the repository and writes 2-5 project-specific agent files into `.loopai/agents/`, then lists every agent file in that directory with its description (pre-existing ones included), flagging files with no description, unparsable frontmatter, or no prompt body instead of listing them as active. It runs with `task_model`, logs to `.loopai/progress/progress-gen-agents.txt`, warns when a file takes a reserved built-in name, and changes nothing else — review the files with `git diff` and commit the useful ones. The flag is standalone: combining it with a plan file, another standalone mode, `--serve`, or `--watch` is an error.

Progress is available at `.loopai/progress/progress-*.txt`; section closures include `<label> took <duration>` lines and runs include a `phase durations:` summary. Commands matching plain, non-checkbox list items after the exact, case-sensitive `## Validation Commands` H2 and before the next heading add per-run lines such as `validation: make test took 42s` and an end-of-run aggregate such as `validation: 2m15s (3 runs)`. The validation aggregate sums command durations and can exceed wall-clock time when commands overlap. Claude uses stream-event arrival time; Codex prefers rollout timestamps and otherwise uses approximate arrival time. Runs without matched command events omit these lines. The dashboard starts with `loopai --serve` and listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` by default; use `--host`, `--port`, or `LOOPAI_WEB_HOST` to change it.

`--worktree` creates a new plan branch from the current `HEAD`, including a non-default branch or detached HEAD, and checks it out under `.loopai/worktrees/<branch>`. When an existing plan branch does not already contain the source `HEAD` seen before any auto-commit, loopai reuses it and automatically merges the source HEAD into it in the fresh worktree. Git 2.38+ predicts conflicts before source mutation; older Git falls back to the real merge and removes the fresh worktree if that merge conflicts. An actual conflict aborts with guidance to merge or rebase the source changes manually. The source checkout must be clean unless `-c`/`--commit` is used; that flag runs `git add -A` and commits all non-ignored changes in the source checkout, advancing its branch or detached `HEAD`, and is a no-op when clean. Branch reuse merges that new source commit through the same synchronization path. An uncommitted plan may be the only change without `--commit` and is then committed in the feature worktree. The flag requires `--worktree`. If the expected worktree already exists and its run lock is free, the same `--worktree` command validates it and automatically continues from the first incomplete task, preserving dirty changes and never syncing or auto-committing the source checkout; supplied `-c`/`--commit` is ignored with a warning. If another loopai process holds the advisory OS lock in the worktree's private Git directory, the command fails immediately with a busy error whose pid and start time are diagnostic only. Process death releases the lock automatically. The removed `--resume-worktree` flag is now an unknown option; rerun with `--worktree`, just as the removed `-c` alias for `--codex-only` was replaced by the long form. Worktree creation does not record a base branch: reviews still diff against `--base-ref`, `default_branch`, or detected `main`/`master`, and merging back to a non-default source requires an explicit base such as `--merge=release/13`. Non-worktree branch mode is unchanged.

Inside cmux, a started implementation or review run leaves a green `done in <elapsed>` status pill on success and a red `failed` pill on non-abort execution failure. Startup/preflight and plan-creation failures do not leave a pill; Ctrl+C clears run status. A later run replaces the pill, and `loopai --clear` removes it explicitly (`--clear` is a successful no-op outside cmux).

Bare `--cmux-workspace` and `--cmux-workspace=always` hand the run off to its own cmux workspace. `--cmux-workspace=auto` keeps the run in the current workspace unless `cmux list-status` contains a `loopai` pill whose text does not start with the final prefix `done` or `failed`; no pill is free. A local auto run whose execution intent is known before config immediately installs a non-final `starting` pill, which the normal reporter replaces after preflight, so later starts detect config, dependency, and worktree setup as busy too. A potentially watch-only `--serve` invocation with no plan or description waits until config resolves its mode, then reserves only if execution will follow; combined `--reset --serve` reserves before its prompt and releases the reservation if config confirms watch-only mode. The optional value must use the attached `=` form. This check is best-effort: query failures, including being outside cmux, quietly run locally (details appear with `--debug`); a stale pill after force-kill can cause one extra workspace, and simultaneous starts can both observe free. On hand-off, loopai creates a workspace named after the branch the run will use (`--branch` override, else the plan-derived name, else `loopai`), relaunches itself there without the flag, prints `handed off to cmux workspace <name>`, and exits. Because the pill key is fixed and the progress bar is per workspace, this is what makes parallel runs independent instead of overwriting each other's status. Unconditional workspace creation remains best-effort: outside cmux or on a refused creation, loopai warns and runs normally in the current terminal. After auto mode positively detects a busy workspace, any pre-spawn refusal or creation failure stops with an error instead of starting a conflicting local run. After a successful hand-off the originating workspace keeps its previous pill. A creation timeout also stops: cmux may already have started the run in the new workspace, so loopai does not duplicate it here. An invocation that could not run anyway is kept in the current terminal in unconditional mode so its error lands where it was typed rather than in a card that closes immediately: a named plan file that does not exist, and a working directory that is not the repository root (a non-git `vcs_command` and a watch-only `--serve`, which run without a `.git` marker, are unaffected). Standalone commands (`--clear`, `--merge`, `--pr`, `--init`, `--dump-defaults`, `--reset` on its own) are never handed off, while `--reset` in front of a plan is performed once in the new workspace; with `--plan` the interactive dialog happens there too. The new workspace runs a fresh shell that inherits nothing from the current terminal, so only `LOOPAI_CONFIG_DIR` and `LOOPAI_WEB_HOST` travel with the command and everything else must come from the shell profile. An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` pass-through requested by either `--preserve-anthropic-api-key` or `preserve_anthropic_api_key` survives the hand-off while the key itself does not, so a key set only in the current terminal is warned about at hand-off.

Close-out commands are standalone modes. `loopai --merge[=base]` requires clean feature and base worktrees (including no untracked files), resolves a missing base as `main` then `master`, merges the current feature branch in the base worktree, overrides squash/no-commit merge defaults, verifies the feature commit was incorporated, safely removes only a clean linked worktree registered for that feature branch, deletes the branch, and clears the pill on success. Ignored files do not count as dirty and are deleted with the linked worktree, so preserve local-only ignored files before merging. `loopai --pr[=base]` requires authenticated `gh` and a GitHub `origin` whose effective push URLs all identify the same repository, pushes committed branch state, creates a PR using the associated plan and diff statistics, keeps the branch/worktree, and clears the pill on success. Commit intended changes before `--pr`; failures retain the pill. Use `=` to supply the optional base value, for example `--merge=release/13`.

Both close-out commands accept an optional positional argument naming the feature, so they can run from the root of the primary checkout or any other registered worktree instead of the feature worktree (a checkout root is still required): a local branch name, a plan basename with or without `.md`, or a plan path. Resolution is deterministic — an exact local branch first, then a plan file in the invoking checkout's `plans_dir` and its `completed/` subdirectory. A located plan resolves to the branch recorded for it under `.loopai/progress/`, so a `--branch` override closes out the branch the run actually created; without a record the branch is derived from the plan filename. The resolved branch must exist locally. It combines with an explicit base, for example `--merge=release/13 dynamic-review-agents`. With an explicit feature, `--merge` merges a branch that is not checked out anywhere and then deletes it without any worktree cleanup; when a feature worktree is registered, the usual cleanliness checks and safe removal still apply, but uncommitted work in an invoking checkout that is neither the feature worktree nor the worktree the merge runs in does not block the merge. The merge runs in the base worktree, or in the primary checkout when the base branch is not checked out anywhere; a feature checked out in the primary checkout while the base occupies a linked worktree is refused, since the merge would have to run in the primary. `--pr <feature>` pushes and opens the PR for a branch that need not be checked out, deriving title and body from the plan as seen from the invoking checkout. A feature resolving to the base branch is an error, as is an identifier matching neither a branch nor a plan, and so is a second positional argument: `--merge release/13 dynamic-review-agents` is the `--merge=release/13 dynamic-review-agents` form with the `=` forgotten and would otherwise close out `release/13` itself. A successful `--merge` names the worktree it removed, since with an explicit feature that directory is not the invoking one.

## Useful options

- `--max-iterations=N`
- `--max-external-iterations=N`
- `--review-patience=N`
- `--task-model=model[:effort]`
- `--review-model=model[:effort]`
- `--external-review-tool=auto|claude|codex|custom|none`
- `--external-review-model=model[:effort]`
- `--external-reviewers=provider[:model[:effort]],...` (mutually exclusive with the two legacy external-review flags)
- `--base-ref=branch-or-commit`
- `-c`, `--commit` (auto-commit the source checkout before creating a fresh worktree; requires `--worktree`)
- `--gen-agents`
- `--clear`
- `--cmux-workspace[=always|auto]` (bare/always always hands off; auto hands off only when the current cmux workspace has an active loopai pill)
- `--merge[=base] [feature]`
- `--pr[=base] [feature]`
- `--wait=duration` (default `10m`; `--wait 0` disables limit retries)
- `--session-timeout=duration`
- `--idle-timeout=duration`
- `--skip-finalize`
- `--preserve-anthropic-api-key`

## Development

```bash
make build
make test
make lint
make fmt
make e2e
GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...
```

Main code:

- `cmd/loopai/` — CLI
- `pkg/config/` — configuration and embedded defaults
- `pkg/executor/` — provider processes
- `pkg/processor/` — task/review pipeline
- `pkg/git/` — Git and worktrees
- `pkg/progress/` — logs
- `pkg/web/` — dashboard

Alternative provider wrappers:

- `scripts/copilot-as-claude/copilot-as-claude.sh` — GitHub Copilot CLI adapter
- `scripts/pi-as-claude/pi-as-claude.sh` — pi CLI adapter; setup and requirements are in `scripts/pi-as-claude/`
- `docs/custom-providers.md` — configuration and protocol details for all included wrappers

## Compatibility boundary

The public product name is loopai. The internal Go module remains `github.com/umputun/ralphex`, and protocol signals remain `<<<RALPHEX:...>>>`. Do not rename either: the module path keeps upstream merges manageable, and stable signals preserve prompt/log compatibility.
